extracted.intended_audience: utilities, cable and broadband providers, pole attachers, small entities, and commenters to the FCC pole-attachment rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: FCC rulemaking (Fourth Report and Order and Further Notice) establishing expedited processes for pole attachment disputes, new utility disclosure requirements, and an Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis describing small-entity impacts and applicable size standards. The document seeks comment on make-ready timelines and contractor/self-help rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and disclosure of cyclical pole inspection reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities must retain copies of their cyclical pole inspection reports and, upon request, provide prospective pole attachers with the information included in the most recent report regarding the poles affected by a prospective attacher’s submitted attachment application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports to be provided include whether any of the affected poles have been "red tagged" by the utility for replacement, and the scheduled replacement date or timeframe. The Commission states this requirement is minimally burdensome because utilities already prepare such reports in the normal course of business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement prior to formal complaint for RBAT review/Accelerated Docket
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties seeking RBAT review and assessment of a dispute and inclusion of a proceeding on the Accelerated Docket must first notify the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau’s Market Disputes Resolution Division (MDRD) by phone and in writing prior to filing the formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This initial notification would constitute the notification required under section 1.736(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT may require pre-filing settlement negotiations or mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rapid Broadband Assessment Team (RBAT) may require that the parties participate, if appropriate, in pre-filing settlement negotiations or mediation under rule 1.737 as a condition for including a matter on the Accelerated Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in pre-filing settlement/mediation can be conditioned on inclusion in the Accelerated Docket to facilitate expedited resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form submission to RBAT for Accelerated Docket consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties seeking both RBAT review and inclusion on the Accelerated Docket must submit a form to RBAT that will elicit information relevant to the scope and nature of the dispute and to whether the dispute is appropriate for expedited mediation and/or placement on the Accelerated Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is intended to provide RBAT with sufficient information to assess suitability for expedited processing; this is characterized as a minimally burdensome requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal-burden principle for new requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: New requirements adopted (e.g., RBAT form and disclosure of existing inspection report information) are to be minimally burdensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission emphasizes requirements merely require parties to submit a form and utilities to provide information they already collect in the normal course of business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require utilities to gather data they do not track
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declined to require utilities to gather and provide pole-related data for matters they do not track in the normal course of business through their inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alternative was rejected as burdensome and unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require utilities to provide pole information prior to application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declined to require that utilities provide new attachers with information about poles prior to the attacher submitting an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: such data would be speculative, the build-out may never occur, and this would impose unnecessary burdens on utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require a single pole-information database or per-utility comprehensive database
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declined to establish a single pole-information database or require each utility to create a database of all its poles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: burdens and costs of creating such databases are considerable given that many utilities own or jointly own poles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require utilities to provide financial data regarding poles and attachment rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declined to require small and other utilities to provide financial data regarding poles and attachment rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: providing such financial data would be overly burdensome for utilities with little or no benefit to broadband deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require utilities to provide detailed age/condition or counts of pending attachment applications per pole
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declined to require small and other utilities to provide information on the age or condition of the poles, or number of current or pending attachment applications for each pole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: could be burdensome, unnecessary, or unfeasible in some cases and would impose significant costs with little or no benefit to broadband deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require more detailed supporting data in make-ready estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declined to require small and other utilities to provide more detailed supporting data in their make-ready estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the current complaint process should be sufficient to address disputes regarding make-ready estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: additional 90 days for make-ready on very large applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Further Notice seeks comment on the tentative conclusion that utilities should have an additional 90 days for make-ready for requests exceeding 3,000 poles or 5 percent of the utility’s poles in a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a proposal for comment, not a final requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: prohibit utilities from limiting application size to avoid timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Further Notice seeks comment on a proposal from NCTA that the Commission revise its rules to prohibit utilities from limiting “the size of an application or the number of poles included in an application so as to avoid the timelines.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking comment on whether such prohibitions should be adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: establish a maximum time for pole owner review of projects of any size
rubrics_metrics.description: Further Notice seeks comment on a proposal that the Commission “establish a maximum time for a pole owner to review projects of any size.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking input on setting an absolute review deadline regardless of project size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: create additional make-ready timeline tiers based on application scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Further Notice seeks comment on whether the Commission should create additional make-ready timeline tiers in its rules to differentiate between attachment applications that could range from requesting access to thousands of poles to tens or even hundreds of thousands of poles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking comment on differentiated timelines by project/pole-count scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: 15-day notification if survey cannot be conducted within 45 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Further Notice seeks comment on a proposal that a utility notify an attacher 15 days after receiving a complete application that it cannot conduct the survey within the required 45-day period so that the attacher can elect self-help for the survey sooner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would enable earlier election of self-help by attachers; Commission seeks comment on feasibility and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: make self-help available for estimate process and ease use of attacher contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Further Notice seeks comment on making self-help available for the estimate process and on whether to amend the Commission’s rules to make it easier for attachers to use their own contractors for self-help and one-touch make-ready when there are no contractors available from a pole owner list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission seeks comment on contractor availability impacts and potential rule changes to facilitate attachers using their own contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standard — Satellite Telecommunications (NAICS 517410)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the SBA’s small business size standard for NAICS 517410, firms with 1,500 or fewer employees are classified as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission estimates approximately 42 providers with 1,500 or fewer employees among providers engaged in satellite telecommunications services; a little more than half can be considered small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standard — All Other Telecommunications (NAICS 517919)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for this industry classifies firms with annual receipts of $35 million or less as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. Census Bureau 2017 data show 1,079 firms in this industry with 1,039 having revenue of less than $25 million; Commission estimates the majority can be considered small.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standard — Cable and Other Subscription Programming (NAICS 515210)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard classifies firms with annual receipts less than $41.5 million as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census data: 378 firms operated in this industry; 149 had revenue less than $25 million; Commission estimates a majority are small.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC small cable company size standard for rate regulation (47 CFR § 76.901(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Commission’s rules, a “small cable company” is one serving 400,000 or fewer subscribers nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on industry data there are about 420 cable companies in the U.S.; of these only seven have more than 400,000 subscribers, so the majority are small under this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC small system size standard (47 CFR § 76.901(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Commission’s rules, a “small system” is a cable system serving 15,000 or fewer subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on industry data, there are about 4,139 cable systems in the U.S.; about 639 have more than 15,000 subscribers; majority are small systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecom Act small cable operator standard and Commission numeric threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The Communications Act defines a “small cable operator” as one that, directly or through an affiliate, serves in the aggregate fewer than one percent of all subscribers in the United States and is not affiliated with entities whose gross annual revenues in the aggregate exceed $250,000,000. The Commission determined that serving fewer than 498,000 subscribers meets this definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on industry data only six cable system operators have more than 498,000 subscribers; Commission notes it does not routinely collect affiliation revenue data and cannot precisely estimate qualifiers under the Act's affiliation prong.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standards for Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution (NAICS 2211 subgroups)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA has established small business size standards for the utility subgroups based on number of employees, ranging from having fewer than 250 employees to having fewer than 1,000 employees, depending on subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census data show 1,693 firms operated in the Electric Power Generation, Transmission and Distribution industry; 1,552 firms had less than 250 employees; Commission concludes majority can be considered small entities under the applicable SBA standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA small business size standard — Wired Telecommunications Carriers (NAICS 517311)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBA small business size standard for Wired Telecommunications Carriers classifies firms having 1,500 or fewer employees as small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2017 Census data show 3,054 firms in this industry with 2,964 operating with fewer than 250 employees; Commission estimates most providers engaged in fixed local services can be considered small under the SBA standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of broadband for classification purposes (>200 kbps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wireline service that terminates at an end user location or mobile device and enables the end user to receive information from and/or send information to the Internet at information transfer rates exceeding 200 kilobits per second (kbps) in at least one direction is classified as a broadband connection under the Commission’s rules (47 CFR § 1.7001(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify providers of wired broadband Internet access service for purposes of the IRFA and industry characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) procedural requirements for IRFA
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA requires the agency to prepare an Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) describing the potential significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities and to solicit written comments on the IRFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written comments must be identified as responses to the IRFA and filed by the deadlines for comments on the Further Notice. The Commission will send a copy of the Further Notice and IRFA to the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the SBA and publish the Further Notice and IRFA (or summaries) in the Federal Register (citations: 5 U.S.C. § 603(a), § 604(b), § 601 et seq.).
